# Visual Storytelling {.unnumbered} ## Overview This chapter challenges students to move beyond default charts and create publication-quality visualizations. You will use AI tools to generate initial code for complex plots in ggplot2 or plotly, and then apply human judgment to refine them for clarity, accuracy, and aesthetics. The lesson emphasizes detecting misleading AI-generated visuals and "steering" the code to tell a truthful and compelling data story. ## Connection Week 5 checked that summaries agree across languages. This week turns a descriptive summary into a visual claim and asks whether the design helps or misleads the audience. Next week you will document the same dataset with EDA and a Table 1. ## Case Study Data Analysis The **NHANES Health Equity data spine** now supports code-reading, EDA, visualization, and reproducibility checks. Use the cached CSV/RDS for routine class work; a CDC retrieval script exists for advanced users. - Cached RDS: `examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.rds` - CSV snapshot: `examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv` - Case-study README: `examples/nhanes-equity/README.md` The default classroom path is to use the cached data so the analysis work is reproducible without internet access. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(readr) library(dplyr) candidate_paths <- c( "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv", "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv" ) nhanes_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1] if (is.na(nhanes_path)) { stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv") } nhanes_analysis <- read_csv(nhanes_path, show_col_types = FALSE) nhanes_analysis |> summarise( rows = n(), missing_bmi = sum(is.na(BMI)), missing_income = sum(is.na(IncomeGroup)) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} nhanes_analysis |> filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), Age >= 20, Age <= 80) |> group_by(IncomeGroup) |> summarise( n = n(), mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1), .groups = "drop" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## In-Class Activity - Work through the [ggplot worked example](worked-example-ggplot.qmd) using the CSV snapshot. - Audit the flawed plot provided in the visual-audit activity and identify at least three issues. - Revise the plot so the title, scale, grouping, and caption support descriptive interpretation. - Explain what changed and why, including any AI assistance you used. Student output: a corrected plot, caption, audit note, and AI-use note. Assignment link: `../../assignments/assignment05-visualization/README.md`. ## Definition of Done - Students can generate, critique, revise, and caption at least one health data visualization. - The activity includes a concrete visual audit checklist. - All example plots render in a fresh Codespace.
